quests.instruction: A worker draws slightly different pictures one after another so that, when they are played quickly, a character seems to move. Who is it?
quests.hint: Think about bringing drawings to life, frame by frame.
quests.explanation: Animators create many pictures with small changes between them. When the pictures are shown quickly, the character appears to move.
quests.funFact: Hand-drawn films can need many pictures for every second of movement.

quests.instruction: Before filming starts, a director sketches the scenes in order, like a comic strip. What is this called?
quests.hint: Think about a picture plan of the story.
quests.explanation: A storyboard shows the main scenes in order, so the film crew can plan shots before filming begins.
quests.funFact: Many animated films use storyboards to test whether a story makes sense before drawing every frame.

quests.instruction: After filming, who chooses the best shots and puts them in order to make the final film?
quests.hint: Think about cutting and joining the pieces of a film.
quests.explanation: Film editors choose the best shots, cut them, and arrange them so that the story flows well.
quests.funFact: A film editor may look at hours of footage to make a short scene.

quests.instruction: A children's book needs pictures that match the story. Who draws them?
quests.hint: Think about the person who draws the pictures for a story.
quests.explanation: Illustrators create pictures that help tell a story or explain an idea.
quests.funFact: Illustrators often read a story carefully to decide what to draw.

quests.instruction: Someone writes the words and the melody of a brand-new song. Who is it?
quests.hint: Think about the person who creates a song from nothing.
quests.explanation: Songwriters invent melodies, words, or both, often trying different ideas before they choose the best one.
quests.funFact: Many songwriters record rough ideas on their phones so they do not forget them.

quests.instruction: Why do writers and artists often make drafts or sketches first?
options: Drafts are always perfect the first time
They can improve ideas before the end
Sketches must never be changed once made
quests.correctAnswer: They can improve ideas before the end
quests.hint: Think about trying ideas out before choosing the best one.
quests.explanation: Drafts and sketches let creators test ideas and make changes before the final version.
quests.funFact: Many famous artworks began as simple pencil sketches.

quests.instruction: Who sketches new clothes, chooses fabrics and colors, and plans how they will be made?
quests.hint: Think about the person who creates the idea for new clothes.
quests.explanation: Fashion designers imagine new clothes, choose materials, and work with makers to turn drawings into real items.
quests.funFact: Fashion designers often make a mini collection of sketches before choosing which pieces to make.

quests.instruction: A company wants a new water bottle that is easy to hold and hard to spill. Who designs it, thinking about how people will use it?
quests.hint: Think about designing everyday objects so they work well.
quests.explanation: Product designers think about how an object looks, feels, and works, and test ideas until the product is easy to use.
quests.funFact: Product designers often watch people use an object to see what could be improved.

quests.instruction: Before making thousands of toys, a designer builds one test version to try out. What is this first test version called?
quests.hint: Think about an early model made for testing.
quests.explanation: A prototype is an early model that lets designers test ideas and fix problems before making many copies.
quests.funFact: A prototype can be made from simple materials like cardboard or foam.

quests.instruction: Who builds the pages and buttons of a website so they work on phones and computers?
quests.hint: Think about someone who makes websites work.
quests.explanation: Web developers write the code that makes websites display and respond properly on different devices.
quests.funFact: Web developers test sites on many screen sizes, from phones to large monitors.

quests.instruction: Why do programmers test a new app before sharing it?
options: To make it run much slower on purpose
To find mistakes before users do
To hide it from every possible user
quests.correctAnswer: To find mistakes before users do
quests.hint: Think about finding problems early.
quests.explanation: Testing helps programmers find mistakes, called bugs, so they can fix them before people use the app.
quests.funFact: Some teams hire testers whose main job is to try to break an app on purpose.

quests.instruction: Who protects computers and online accounts from people who try to break in?
quests.hint: Think about keeping information safe online.
quests.explanation: Cyber security experts look for weaknesses in computer systems and put protections in place, such as strong passwords and updates.
quests.funFact: Using a long, unique password for each account is one of the simplest ways to stay safe online.

quests.instruction: An electronics technician builds a simple circuit with a battery, wires, and a bulb. What must be true for the bulb to light?
options: The bulb must be much heavier
The wire must make a full loop
The wire must be cut in two
quests.correctAnswer: The wire must make a full loop
quests.hint: Think about a path for electricity to travel all the way around.
quests.explanation: A circuit needs a complete path from the battery, through the bulb, and back, so electricity can flow.
quests.funFact: A switch turns a circuit on or off by completing or breaking the loop.

quests.instruction: A door opens by itself when someone walks near it. Which part notices the person?
quests.hint: Think about a part that detects something.
quests.explanation: Sensors detect things such as movement, light, or heat and tell the machine when to act.
quests.funFact: Sensors are also used in phone screens, cars, and weather stations.

quests.instruction: Who designs, builds, and tests machines that can do tasks such as lifting boxes in a warehouse?
quests.hint: Think about people who make machines that follow instructions.
quests.explanation: Robotics engineers combine mechanics, electronics, and computer code to create machines that can do tasks.
quests.funFact: Many robots follow instructions called programs, just like apps on a phone.

quests.instruction: A 3D printer makes an object by doing what?
options: Stacking very thin layers on top
Carving it from a giant rock by hand
Pouring it from a bucket of paint
quests.correctAnswer: Stacking very thin layers on top
quests.hint: Think about building up an object from the bottom.
quests.explanation: A 3D printer builds an object layer by layer from a digital design, which is useful for models and prototypes.
quests.funFact: Some 3D printers can make parts that fit together in a single piece.

quests.instruction: A map app finds routes by comparing roads, distances, and traffic. Which worker designs this kind of software?
quests.hint: Think about someone who writes programs.
quests.explanation: Software developers write the instructions that let apps work out routes and show them on a screen.
quests.funFact: Map apps update their routes using information about traffic and road closures.

quests.instruction: A farm drone flies over fields taking pictures. Who controls it from the ground?
quests.hint: Think about someone who flies a small aircraft from the ground.
quests.explanation: Drone pilots guide drones using remote controls or screens, and they follow safety rules about where it is safe to fly.
quests.funFact: Drones often have rules about how high and how close to people they may fly.

quests.instruction: A graphic designer chooses calm blue and green colors for a hospital poster. Why?
options: Because blue and green are cheaper
Calm colors can help people relax
quests.correctAnswer: Calm colors can help people relax
quests.hint: Think about how colors can change feelings.
quests.explanation: Designers choose colors on purpose because colors can affect how people feel when they look at something.
quests.funFact: Designers often test several color choices before deciding.

quests.instruction: A drummer and a guitarist practice a song together many times. What are they working on?
options: Playing in time with each other
Making the room a little warmer
quests.correctAnswer: Playing in time with each other
quests.hint: Think about two instruments sounding like one band.
quests.explanation: Rehearsing helps musicians match rhythm and timing so that they sound like one band.
quests.funFact: Bands often practice difficult parts slowly first and then speed up.

quests.instruction: A photographer waits for the soft light just after sunrise. Why?
options: Because the sun makes cameras louder
Soft light makes pictures look gentle
Because dark nights are always better
quests.correctAnswer: Soft light makes pictures look gentle
quests.hint: Think about how light changes through the day.
quests.explanation: Soft light has fewer harsh shadows, so it can make a photograph look smooth and gentle.
quests.funFact: Photographers call the hour after sunrise and before sunset the golden hour.

quests.instruction: Who plans the rules, levels, and challenges of a video game so it is fun to play?
quests.hint: Think about someone who decides how a game works.
quests.explanation: Game designers decide the rules, goals, and challenges, then test them to see if the game is fun.
quests.funFact: Game designers often ask players to test early versions and give feedback.

quests.instruction: Before cutting expensive cloth, a clothing maker cuts a paper shape to check the fit. Why?
options: To waste as much cloth as possible
To make the cloth feel heavier
To test the shape cheaply first
quests.correctAnswer: To test the shape cheaply first
quests.hint: Think about avoiding costly mistakes.
quests.explanation: A paper pattern lets makers test shapes and fit with cheap materials before cutting the real cloth.
quests.funFact: Pattern makers often adjust paper shapes many times before using fabric.

quests.instruction: A film shows a door creaking open slowly. Who creates and records special sounds like this for films?
quests.hint: Think about someone who makes sounds for a story.
quests.explanation: Sound designers create or record sounds, from footsteps to creaking doors, that help a film feel real.
quests.funFact: Some film sounds are made with surprising objects, such as celery to imitate breaking bones.

quests.instruction: A museum wants a touch screen that lets visitors explore a painting. Which pair of jobs would work together?
options: Underwater welder and ice cream seller
Coal miner and school crossing guard
quests.hint: Think about one job for the screen and one for the look.
quests.explanation: A software developer builds the touch screen program and a graphic designer makes it clear and attractive.
quests.funFact: Digital displays in museums often need artists, programmers, and historians working together.

quests.instruction: A designer shows her draft to others and asks what is unclear. What is she doing?
options: Throwing the draft away at once
quests.hint: Think about asking others for ideas.
quests.explanation: Feedback gives creators new ideas and shows what is confusing, so they can improve their work.
quests.funFact: Many creators ask people who have never seen their work, because they notice different things.

quests.instruction: A potter, a woodworker, and a jeweler all make objects by hand. What are workers like this often called?
quests.hint: Think about skilled makers who work by hand.
quests.explanation: Artisans are skilled makers who create objects by hand, such as pottery, furniture, or jewelry.
quests.funFact: Many artisans learn their skills over many years of practice.

quests.instruction: Which job needs both creative ideas and technical knowledge of how things work?
quests.hint: Think about designing buildings that look good and stay standing.
quests.explanation: Architects imagine how a building will look and also need to understand structure and safety so it works.
quests.funFact: Architects often use computer models to show clients how a building will look.

quests.instruction: A school app is being made. Which order is sensible?
options: Share it, test it, build it, sketch it
Sketch the idea, build it, test it, share it
Test it, share it, sketch it, build it
quests.correctAnswer: Sketch the idea, build it, test it, share it
quests.hint: Think about planning before building and testing before sharing.
quests.explanation: Teams sketch an idea first, build a version, test it for problems, and then share it with users.
quests.funFact: Teams often repeat the build and test steps several times before sharing.

quests.instruction: Which statement best shows how technical and creative workers help each other?
options: Each skill helps the other make ideas real
Creative workers never need any technology
Technical workers should never have ideas
quests.correctAnswer: Each skill helps the other make ideas real
quests.hint: Think about the many projects in this course that need both.
quests.explanation: Creative ideas need technical knowledge to become real, and technical work often needs creative ideas to find new solutions.
quests.funFact: Many modern jobs, such as game design and architecture, use both kinds of skills.
